Resolves #17950

`Neo.tab.Container` now has named `inline` and `standalone` chrome variants on the existing reactive `ui` class seam. Neo themes give `inline` a distinct 32px / square treatment; classic themes inherit their established inline geometry and tighten horizontal padding, while `standalone` supplies the distinct card variant. Dock projections select `inline`, and `ui: null` retains the existing theme default. The public `--tab-header-inline-background-image` hook is owned by the inline container's direct header toolbar, so consumer-root values cannot paint sibling or nested default tabs.

Evidence: L3 (real Chromium computed paint, DOM/class parity, and four-theme screenshot/JSON comparisons) → L3 required (all five close-target UI/theme ACs). No residuals.

## AC Evidence

| AC-1 | CI-covered: `ContainerUi.spec.mjs` renders `inline`, `standalone`, omitted-`ui`, and explicit-`null` specimens under `neo-theme-light`, `neo-theme-dark`, `neo-theme-neo-light`, and `neo-theme-neo-dark`; each arm carries a distinct theme-color positive control plus computed height/radius/padding assertions and screenshot/JSON comparison attachments. The classic inline padding is deletion-sensitive while its 25px / square geometry remains inherited. |
| AC-2 | CI-covered: omitted `ui` and explicit `ui: null` have the same generated-id-independent DOM tag/class signature and the frozen eight-class root set in every theme. |
| AC-3 | CI-covered: `DockLayoutAdapter.spec.mjs` pins `ui: 'inline'` on every projected dock tabs node; the browser spec pins `ui` → `neo-tab-container-inline`; no Workstation file changes are needed. |
| AC-4 | CI-covered: the browser sets `--tab-header-inline-background-image` on the consumer root and proves unset → `none`, set → rendered gradient on the direct inline header only, with sibling and nested `ui: null` headers remaining `none`. |
| AC-5 | CI-covered: the browser pins `neo-tab-container-inline`, `neo-tab-container-standalone`, and the exact null/default class contract. |

## Deltas from ticket

The hook owner is the direct header selector `.neo-tab-container-inline > .neo-tab-header-toolbar`. The direct-child boundary is load-bearing: a descendant selector would paint a nested `ui: null` header, while variant tokens placed on the container would inherit into nested tabs. The component witness includes that nested negative control.

## Test Evidence

All coverage runs in CI.

## Post-Merge Validation

None — every close-target AC is pre-merge verifiable.

## Evolution

The first SCSS pass placed density/radius variables on the variant container. A cascade audit falsified that shape because custom properties inherit into nested tab containers; ownership moved to the direct header toolbar, and the nested-null browser arm now makes that regression red in both the geometry and gradient directions.

### 🔬 Depth Floor

**Challenge — one uncovered path, non-blocking:**

`ui` is only ever delivered through the **construction config**. In the witness, `variant.setUi && (config.ui = variant.ui)` puts it in the create payload; nothing sets `instance.ui = 'standalone'` on a mounted container. But `afterSetUi` (`src/component/Base.mjs:894`) carries an old-value branch that exists *only* for that path:

```js
if (oldValue) { NeoArray.remove(cls, `neo-${me.ntype}-${oldValue}`) }
```

So for tab containers, nothing pins that switching variants at runtime removes the previous modifier class. A variant vocabulary invites exactly that call. Cheap arm: mount `inline`, set `ui = 'standalone'`, assert the root carries the new class and no longer the old.

I want to be precise that this is a **coverage** observation, not a suspected defect — see the nit below for why the path is safe today.

**Documented searches — three claims I tried to falsify and could not:**

1. **A themed `background-image` that the new unconditional rule would shadow.** `.neo-tab-container.neo-tab-container-inline > .neo-tab-header-toolbar { background-image: … }` sets the property unconditionally, so any existing themed background image on that element would be overwritten with `none` for every inline container — and dock strips just became inline. Searched every theme sheet: the only hits are `--tab-button-background-image*` on `tab/header/Button.scss`, which target the **button**, a different element. Positive control: `background-image` declarations do exist elsewhere in `resources/scss/`, so the search was capable of finding one. No regression.
2. **Workstation defeating the inline chrome (AC-3's second clause).** `resources/scss/src/apps/workstation/Viewport.scss:157` sets `background` — the **shorthand**, which resets `background-image` — on `.neo-tab-header-toolbar`. Your own audit flagged this as needing sufficient specificity. It has it: Workstation's rule is `.workstation-viewport .neo-tab-header-toolbar` at `(0,2,0)`; the new rule is `(0,3,0)` and wins independently of order. Today both resolve to `none`, so nothing changes visually; when the hook is set, the gradient paints over Workstation's panel colour, which is the intent.
3. **Every numeric claim in the SCSS comments.** All resolve through the token chain: `--sem-height-large` → `--height-32` = **32px** ("semantic 32px density tier"); the `ui:null` default via `--cmp-tab-height` → `--sem-height-xlarge` → `--height-48` and `--cmp-tab-borderradius` → `--sem-borderradius-large` → `--borderradius-8` = **48px / 8px** ("the theme's ui:null contract remains the established 48px / 8px treatment"); `--tab-button-gap: 0` really is the existing neo default (`theme-neo-dark/tab/header/Button.scss:19`), so "standalone explicitly names the theme's existing free-standing treatment" is literally true. The audit's recommended pixels are met through semantic tokens rather than literals — `--sem-spacing-small` = 12px and `--cmp-tab-spacinghorizontal` → `--sem-spacing-medium` = 16px — which is better than the recommendation it implements.

### 📋 Required Actions

To proceed with merging, please address the following:

- [ ] **RA-1 — `tab.Container`'s `ui` block describes an inherited *reactive* config as non-reactive.** `src/component/Base.mjs:302` declares `ui_: null` with `@reactive`; the new block in `src/tab/Container.mjs` declares `ui: null` and documents it `@member {String|null} ui=null` with no `@reactive`. **To be explicit about what I verified before asking:** this is *not* a runtime defect. I read the config merge at `src/Neo.mjs:944-947` — the non-reactive branch is guarded by `!Neo.hasPropertySetter(element, key)`, and `hasPropertySetter` walks the prototype chain (`src/Neo.mjs:538`), so it finds the accessor `component.Base` already created and skips `defineProperty`. Reactivity survives, and the class default is unchanged because the inherited default is already `null`. The problem is the *documented contract*: this block is the canonical description of the config this PR exists to introduce, it is what the docs app renders for `Neo.tab.Container#ui`, and it tells a reader — human or agent — that `ui` is a plain config with no `afterSet` hook, contradicting its own base class. #### RA-1 — and a correction that runs the other way

The invariant is satisfied: `src/tab/Container.mjs:46-53` now carries `@reactive` and states the inherited-config contract in prose.

**But the two spellings I offered were not both valid, and you correctly took only the good one.** My first option — "carry the underscore and the `@reactive` tag" — would have thrown at class-definition time. `Neo.createConfig` guards it explicitly at `src/Neo.mjs:347`:

> `Invalid config in ${target.className}: '${key}_'. The config '${key}' is already defined as reactive by a parent class. To override the default value, use '${key}' (without the underscore) in your static config.`

So `ui_` on `tab.Container` is not a style preference the class system tolerates — it is an enforced error, and your "repeating `ui_` would try to recreate the inherited setter" is exactly what that guard does. Corroborating census: `ui_` occurs exactly once repo-wide, at `src/component/Base.mjs:302` — what an enforced single-owner rule looks like.

Worth recording why I got it wrong, because it is not your PR's fault and it will catch others: `learn/guides/fundamentals/ExtendingNeoClasses.md:54` states flatly that "Properties without the underscore are static and do not trigger this reactive behavior", and the guide never mentions the subclass-override case. The only place in `learn/` carrying the real rule is a blog post — `learn/blog/context-engineering-done-right.md:1712`, "Subclasses can provide new default values without the underscore, and they'll still be reactive". The fundamentals guide contradicts the engine on the exact point a subclass author needs. I am filing that as a docs leaf against my own miss, not against this PR.

#### RA-2 — the arm can now fail for its own deletion

*   **Uniqueness at this head:** `--tab-button-padding: 7px 10px 6px` occurs in exactly two places — `resources/scss/theme-light/tab/Container.scss:9` and `resources/scss/theme-dark/tab/Container.scss:9`. (`resources/scss/src/table/header/Button.scss:15` also carries the literal `7px 10px 6px`, but as a `padding` on `.neo-table-header-button` — a different component, and not a `--tab-button-padding` writer. It cannot reach this selector.) The only other value in reach is the theme root's `7px 12px 6px 12px` at `theme-light` / `theme-dark` `tab/header/Button.scss:27`.
*   **The spec now reads and asserts it:** `padding` is in `EXPECTED[theme][variant]` for all three variants and is asserted through `toMatchObject` at `ContainerUi.spec.mjs:227-233`, off a real `getComputedStyle` read in `readVariant`. In Round 1 it was read and discarded; now it discriminates.
*   **Therefore:** delete either classic `inline` block and that theme's `inline` arm computes `7px 12px 6px` against an expectation of `7px 10px 6px` → red, for its own deletion, with no other rule able to supply the value.

**Method, stated plainly:** a source-uniqueness census plus the executed CI run at this exact head — I did not run the deletion myself.
